anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: the initial numeric 2 persists course deliver plus both caps before any write, waves 1 and 2 run with fresh helpers and closure review with no intermediate menu, the deadline table renews only on own pushes (12:17, 12:25, 12:27) while the 12:11 base-only observation is explicitly 'not renewed', BEHIND queues the loop sync without a new pick, and final offers merge without executing merge or approval. Checkpoint B keeps the no-progress exit Before already had (that fact held in both), C now shows the authorized in-progress re-run being watched despite the open CI P1 and resolved by fresh closure with no spent round, and D correctly separates repair.wave.sync.pre_head=B from expected_remote_head=A, leases against A, and restores clean B. Before failed f1/f2/f3 by refusing the deliver course and rendering wait/update-branch menus, f5 by omitting the single authorized re-run and its watch gating, and f6 by labelling A as both lease and pre_head. Nothing in After regressed a fact Before held; keep the explicit 'persisted before sync/rebase' annotations and the lease-vs-restore distinction in the D table, and keep the base-observation row separate from push rows, since those are what make f2, f4 and f6 legible to a reader.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before refused the course model outright ("deliver is not a supported menu verb"), so it never ran repairs, pushes, deadlines, the BEHIND sync, the C watch, or the D restore/lease handling, and its B exit was motivated by missing authority rather than the repeated-red/source-change rule; every fact failed there. After delivers the Change cleanly: the single initial `2` persists course deliver, P1 and CI-minted P2 are repaired in-sequence with no intermediate menu, deadlines 12:17/12:25/12:27 are tabulated with the 12:11 base observation explicitly marked "not a push", BEHIND triggers the sync with no decision, final offers merge but the stop pick executes nothing, B exits on repeated red with the base-sync SHA ruled out, C admits the bounded watch over the in-progress re-run and resolves P1 by fresh closure with usage 0/10 unchanged, and D stores pre_head B and expected_remote_head A, leases against A, and restores clean B without a second push. Two small wording points to tighten so the facts stay unambiguous: in the 12:02 row say "the own push opens the window" rather than "the first admitted watch opens the window" (the fact ties renewal to pushes, not watches), and add a short clause such as "fresh helper per repair, closure review before each push" to the repair rows so f1's "fresh helpers and closure review" is stated rather than implied; also consider recording in D that the sync spend is persisted at the push attempt, since the table currently books it at rebase time.
